On the 15th of this month, officers from the National Security Department of the police searched Garden Books and Stay Books, arresting two people from Garden Books and three from Stay Books. They were accused of allegedly violating Article 24 of the Safeguarding National Security Ordinance, which concerns "acts with seditious intent done with a seditious intention." National security police seized books and other items from the two bookstores. It is understood that the book in question is *Only Red Flowers Bloom: Identity and Belonging in the Xi Jinping Era*, written by Feng Zheyun.

Garden Books was established in 1976 by Wong Sheung-wai, who had returned to Hong Kong from studying in Taiwan that year. It is a long-standing second-floor bookstore in Hong Kong, with a shop space of approximately 600 square feet, floor-to-ceiling bookshelves, and a collection of tens of thousands of books. It specialises in literature, history, and philosophy titles, and also publishes and distributes books. Some of its content involves mainland Chinese politics, including books commonly known as mainland "banned books."

In the 1990s, the book *The Private Life of Chairman Mao* sold extremely well. According to an interview with Wong Sheung-wai by Initium Media in 2016, Garden Books imported 300,000 copies of the book, with a net profit of HK$1.95 million per title. According to records, the book was written by Li Zhisui, who served as Mao Zedong's personal physician from 1954 to 1976. The book recorded his observations of Mao in daily life, as well as inside stories of the Chinese Communist Party's senior leadership at the time. Garden Books also published Zhou Lunzuo's *The Truth About the Cultural Revolution Rebel Faction* in 2006, and *The Cultural Revolution: Historical Truth and Collective Memory*, edited by Song Yongyi, in 2007.

Garden Books is the third local independent bookstore to announce its closure in recent months. Earlier this month, longtime Hong Kong Book Fair exhibitors Yulin Bookstore and Lok Man Bookstore were suddenly disqualified from participating by the Hong Kong Trade Development Council. Yulin Bookstore subsequently announced on social media on the 8th of this month that it would "gloriously end its retail operations" when its lease expires next April.

Less than a week after Yulin Bookstore announced its closure, Stay Books, founded in 2022 by veteran media professional Sham Wan-wah and others, also announced on the 14th of this month that it would close on 30 August. Stay Books stated at the time that an elusive "red line" was one of the reasons for its closure. One day after Stay Books announced its closure (the 15th), national security police conducted an arrest operation, searching Stay Books and Garden Books and arresting a total of five people. They were accused of allegedly violating Article 24 of the Safeguarding National Security Ordinance, which concerns "acts with seditious intent done with a seditious intention." The case was referred to the police National Security Department by the Customs and Excise Department, which stated that books with seditious intent had been discovered in a shipment sent from outside the territory to Hong Kong. Following the incident, Stay Books did not open for business, and members of the public left messages of encouragement outside the door.
